matrix.scope: Four independently reported profile pairs across three frozen protocols; neither the original v3 eight-run nor v3b six-run matrix completed

measurementNotes: Per-child lifetime peaks include startup. The live-set measure is a post-major-GC observational upper bound, not an exact retained-set measurement.

Tree RSS is the maximum sampled sum for the daemon and its observed descendants, including ACP children and local MCP processes where present. Shared pages may be counted repeatedly; this is neither unique physical memory nor a continuous peak measurement.
GC deltas use each PID/start-ticks generation between fresh workload-start and before-teardown responses, including inter-turn waits. Aggregate child maxima are never subtracted.
The collector also issues full status and per-turn context-usage/session-status diagnostics. Their allocation/CPU overhead is included in the measurements and has not been separately benchmarked.

The tap observes existing RPC traffic without adding resource requests or forcing GC. Request IDs are paired internally but not serialized; offline framing tests validate pairing while raw audit verifies recorded times and generations.
File pages and MCP text are independently reconstructed and matched; answer semantics are not graded. Delivered bytes do not prove all history remains resident.
Context usage is recorded as reported by the daemon, including its estimate marker. Token decreases and explicit events are reported without inferring unrecorded compaction.

MCP data is deterministic repetitive synthetic text from three local stdio servers. Legacy clientCount=0 coexists with three connected pooled entries; the pool and process evidence supplies the cardinality.

The accepted v3c concurrent pair uses the four existing full repositories ws000 through ws003, verified identical commit, target files and absent workspace settings with unchanged before/after state. The excluded v3b concurrency attempt used longer temporary copy paths. Four overlapping prompt intervals and active-prompt observations are required.

The retained v3 long pair, v3b MCP/multi pairs and new v3c concurrency pair have different collector/prompt/workspace protocols and are separately attributed. One pair per profile is screening only. Provider/model variability prevents attributing wall-clock differences to the heap ceiling or defining acceptable regression thresholds.
These runs do not establish a universal 544 MiB grant, maximum supported concurrency, production RSS safety, multi-hour stability, Node 24 compatibility, or 8/32 GiB deployment capacity.
excluded: Earlier v1/v2/v2b batches are separate protocols and not pooled into these screens.

v3 run3 multi/544 ended 10 prompts and 11 tools but only 9 turns passed the frozen contract; the tenth requested page was complete and then an extra Glob caused rejection. No final fresh workload report exists. The attempt and the original incomplete matrix remain excluded; v3b restarts all three missing profile pairs with only read_file exposed and a narrower reading instruction.

v3b run5 concurrent/544 had four end_turns and five calls: one failed read used a model-mistyped long path (permission provenance), then all four required pages were delivered correctly. Failed/extra call criteria stopped the matrix; no final resource window exists. v3c restarts only the concurrency pair using verified existing short repository paths without changing prompts or weakening body/count validation.
Linux startup-only preflight batches are excluded. The initial MCP preflight failed an incorrect legacy clientCount expectation, not service discovery or heap exhaustion.

decision.interpretation: Keep 544 MiB as an experimental candidate for repeated and broader partition/Node calibration; do not infer production admission readiness from this single-pair screen.
